mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of GDPC1 decline episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly lower during UNRATE > 6.5% episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which increases input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of such INDPRO contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) below the prior three-month average signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 3-month average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly lower during HOUST collapse episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (i.e., stable or rising unemployment despite rising employment) signals a shift toward lower-wage, part-time employment, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases month-over-month AND UNRATE increases month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during episodes where PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise month-over-month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 5-year average signals reduced household buffer and higher consumption financed by debt, which increases default risk and uncertainty, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly lower during prolonged RSAFS decline episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
